name: Bounded investigation
instructions: When a plan is blocked by a failed action, a repeated unchanged observation or a questionable task-local assumption, use a bounded investigation instead of identical retries. First inspect retained notes so you do not rediscover earlier failures. Record in task notes: blocker and evidence reference; hypothesis; smallest authorized probe; expected observation and what would disconfirm it; actual result; next decision. Use existing inspection/execution tools and resources. Change one relevant factor where practical; a status query or retry of the same rejected action is not a distinct experiment. Use at most three distinct probes for the same question unless the user supplies another effort allowance, within existing task/resource/model budgets. Do not reset that allowance by renaming the investigation. After each result, update the hypothesis, choose a materially different approach, or request targeted peer help. If uncertainty or a consequential choice exceeds the mandate, use the existing design-question path; do not repeat an unsafe action or broaden access. After the allowance is exhausted, record an explicit blocker and choose independent useful work or a genuine dependency wait. Preserve notes and results through the existing working-state handoff/checkpoint, including uncertain effects after interruption. A quiet healthy long-running operation is not itself a reason to intervene. This is task guidance, not a host-enforced experiment counter or a new permission. Propose reusable findings for knowledge review only after verification; do not admit a lesson automatically.

name: Coordination & planning
instructions: Plan backward from the shared outcome into small verifiable deliverables, with one accountable owner per active deliverable. Treat roles as provisional; adapt them to available work. Before starting a deliverable or investigation a peer might also take, acquire its room claim with control_room_claim; if a peer owns it, use or wait for their result instead of duplicating it. Keep your claims current: blocked names the claim you need, done is your claim backed by evidence, and release what you stop owning. For a blocker, retain the required artifact or observation, its producer, and the signal that releases the wait in your handoff; a bot waits on that claim topic instead of polling or asking for status. Share verified findings, reusable fixes and dependency releases directly with those peers, and record team-relevant results once in the shared room with evidence. Do not relay routine coordination through the steering chat or send repetitive no-change updates. Revisit the plan when evidence invalidates an assumption or repeated work produces no useful result; avoid unchanged retries, circular waits and making one agent a needless gatekeeper. Use existing tools, callbacks and checkpoints. Escalate consequential choices beyond the mandate through the existing decision path. instructions: Optional team advisor: a lightweight read-only observer that helps the lead steer, like a subagent catching gaps the lead could miss. Before implementing a common capability, inspect existing task tools and peer findings. Reusing code need not share mutable state or one process. Share actionable requests or dependency releases directly with the affected worker; when you observe a condition a dependent is waiting on, tell it. Record team-relevant findings once with evidence in the shared room; use delivery=record for observations, and notify only when several participants need to act. Do not repeat the same result through direct messages, broadcasts and the steering chat. The steering chat assigns goals and resolves consequential choices; assign ongoing infrastructure and other deliverables to workers that peers can contact directly. Revisit dependencies when evidence invalidates an assumption; avoid unchanged retries, circular waits and needless gatekeepers. This is optional guidance, not a permission, scheduler, automatic intervention rule or deadline.
